newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New NZ cyclone more severe than Fergus - forecasts.
newsitem.headline: New NZ cyclone more severe than Fergus - forecasts.

text.p: Northern parts of New Zealand affected by last month's Cyclone Fergus should brace for an even more severe period of high wind and torrential rain as Cyclone Drena approaches the country on Friday, forecasters said on Thursday.
MetService chief meteorologist Augie Auer said Northland and parts of the Auckland region could expect about 200 mm of rainfall over an 18-hour period starting on Friday morning.
The Coromandel peninsula was forecast to receive about 300 mm. Winds gusting up to 130km/hour would also strike as the storm passed down the west coast of the North Island.
"This is a dangerous storm," Auer told Radio New Zealand.
Auer advised campers in the north of the country to pack up and leave.
"Certainly over the next 24 hours I think anyone in Northland, Bay of Islands, even in some of the recreational areas of Auckland district will need to be moving out.

"Coromandel will cop it again. You might get away with spending another night in the Coromandel before you have to move out tomorrow morning, but that's cutting it pretty close and if it were me, I'd be moving out as well. I just think it's all going downhill pretty quick," he said.
Auer said the cyclone would track down the west of the country and have more impact on populous areas than the remnants of Cyclone Fergus, which struck shortly before the New Year.
Fergus is estimated to have caused up to NZ$2 million worth of damage as it washed out roads, closed bridges and affected water supplies.
Auer said heavy rainfall in Northland would start around 3 a.m. on Friday, continuing for 18 hours as the storm passed.
Auckland was expected to be hit worst from around 6 a.m. onwards, with 100 mm of rainfall expected to fall on most of the city over the 18-hour period.
Northeasterly winds would make the city particularly vulnerable and the Auckland Harbour Bridge could be dangerous as winds of around 90 km/hour buffeted the city.
The Coromandel's rainfall blitz would be at its peak from around mid-morning.
Auer said by noon Saturday the storm was forecast to be centred just off the coast from Wanganui. That region and Taranaki could also expect heavy rainfall as it passed through.
